articles.title: Happy 80th Jim!!
articles.summary: SJAA members surprised long-time member Jim Van Nuland with an 80th birthday party at their October 15th general meeting, celebrating his significant contributions to the club over 30 years. His extensive service includes running the School Star Party Program, serving as Club Secretary for two decades, and managing annual auctions and calendars.

articles.title: 2016 Ends with Three Supermoons
articles.summary: The article details the occurrence of three supermoons at the close of 2016, defining the term as a full moon coinciding with the Moon's perigee. It highlights the November 14 supermoon as the closest of the 21st century and notes that the December 14 supermoon will significantly hinder viewing of the Geminid meteor shower. The piece also explains the visual effects of supermoons, including their increased brightness and the "moon illusion."

articles.title: Planet Orbiting Nearby Star Could be Habitable
articles.summary: A French-American research team's simulations suggest that Proxima b, a recently discovered exoplanet orbiting Proxima Centauri, could be habitable with the potential for liquid water on its surface. Located in its star's habitable zone, the planet may possess a rocky or even an entirely ocean-covered surface, providing a foundation for future habitability studies. Additionally, the article includes a brief observation from the Hubble Space Telescope of the dwarf irregular galaxy NGC 4789A.

articles.title: OSA Coyote Valley Harvest Festival September 10, 2016
articles.summary: The article reports on the successful OSA Coyote Valley Harvest Festival held on September 10, 2016, where volunteers from SJAA engaged over 1200 visitors with solar telescopes and activities like UV bead bracelet making. It highlights the use of a 19" monitor and Mallincam Sky-Raider camera, powered for over five hours, which proved suitable for future outreach events. The report also briefly mentions a prior solar party at the Cambrian Festival.

articles.title: SJAA Member Observation Posts and Reports
articles.summary: This article presents multiple observation reports from SJAA members, including Sukhada Palav's visit to an astronomy program at Glacier National Park and Marilyn Perry's review of Vixen wide-field binoculars and her observation of the Moon-Aldebaran conjunction and an 89 Tau occultation. Gary Chock also provides a detailed account of the 2016 Oregon Star Party, noting observing conditions, facilities, and reconnaissance for the 2017 Total Solar Eclipse.

articles.title: Kid Spot
articles.summary: This article, titled "Kid Spot," presents astronomy-related content designed for children, featuring a collection of space-themed jokes and an interactive quiz. It also includes a "Did You Know?" section that provides various intriguing facts about celestial bodies, space exploration milestones, and significant figures and discoveries in astronomy.

articles.title: From the Board of Directors
articles.summary: The Board of Directors announces several upcoming events and key dates for the club. These include the availability of 2017 RASC handbooks and calendars, a bi-annual swap meet, rescheduled December meeting, a Show-n-Tell event, the annual Pot Luck dinner and Awards Ceremony, and officer elections in March 2017 with two open board seats.

articles.title: Board Meeting Excerpts
articles.summary: The SJAA Board meetings from August to October 2016 addressed various operational and programmatic initiatives. Key decisions included funding the Dr. Robert Armstrong ASP Scholarship, approving a $4,300 budget to expand the member loaner telescope program, and allocating funds for community outreach events and RASC guidebooks. Discussions also covered improving member engagement, developing online member management tools, and facility maintenance and upgrades.

articles.title: SJAA Library and Programs
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) offers diverse resources and programs for its members and the wider community, from beginners to experienced enthusiasts. These include educational sessions like Quick STARt and Intro to the Night Sky, practical support through Telescope Fix It sessions and an equipment loaner program, and specialized groups for astro imaging. SJAA also provides a library of astronomy materials and hosts regular observing events such as Solar Observing and Town Star Parties.
